newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica seeks kidnappers after Dutch pair freed.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica seeks kidnappers after Dutch pair freed.

text.p: Costa Rican police said on Wednesday they were on the trail of kidnappers who released a Dutch couple on Tuesday after receiving a reported $600,000 ransom.

The search began immediately after the husband and wife were freed about 6 p.m. local time (midnight GMT), when police got a glimpse of the kidnappers and exchanged gunfire with them for 10 minutes, Manuel Alvarado, director of Costa Rica's Judicial Police, told reporters.
Two Dutch citizens who operate a tree farm in northern Costa Rica, Hurte Sierd Zylstra and Jetsi Hendrika, both 50 years hold, were seized from the farm late Aug. 24 or early Aug. 25.
Police did not say who paid the ransom nor how much it was, nor did they deny unofficial reports that $600,000 was paid.

At the time of the abduction, the kidnappers had Zylstra and Hendrika leave a note for a third Dutch citizen, Ebe Huizinga, who owns the teak tree farm. Huizinga arrived in Costa Rica shortly after the abduction but no further details were available, police said.
The release was negotiated by a local Roman Catholic priest, Eduardo Bolanos, and a Nicaraguan named Esteban Paiz who worked for the Dutch pair, police said.

Zylstra and Hendrika were taken from the same general area from where a German tourist and a Swiss tour guide were kidnapped earlier in the year. Those two were held for 71 days before being released when relatives paid a $200,000 ransom.

Former Nicaraguan guerrillas were charged with the earlier kidnapping and a similar group has been suspected in this case. A group calling itself the "Maria Felix" commando had demanded $1.5 million for the Dutch pair's release.
Alvarado said dozens of police officers aided by helicopters and search dogs were combing the area near the Nicaraguan border where the hostages were released.
They are searching for at least five men who appeared to be heading north toward Nicaragua, Alvarado said. One of the men might be injured, he said.

A police source who asked not to be indentified said authorities believe all five kidnappers are Nicaraguans, identifying two of them as the brothers, one of whom worked at a plantation next to the tree farm.
Costa Rica has asked for help from Nicaragua in rounding up the suspects.
Meanwhile, Zylstra and Hendrika received medical exams and were interrogated by authorities. They had yet to make any statements to the press.
